source.title: ICRP Publication 89: Basic Anatomical and Physiological Data for Use in Radiological Protection: Reference Values
source.obtained_from: ICRP website, free to download under the Free the Annals Initiative (reuse needs ICRP permission; only individual values are recorded here, with citation).
source.storage: Kept on the platform owner's computer; not committed.
source.extraction: AI-assisted from the PDF text layer (pdftotext -layout); each value checked against the extracted text of the cited page. Independent review pending.

applies_to: Reference adult male (ICRP Reference Man), resting, recumbent. Not a patient value.

cardiac_output_adult_male.location: Table 2.39 (printed page 28, PDF page 42); Section 7.5, paragraph 311 (PDF page 153)
cardiac_output_adult_male.basis: Trimmed means of more than 50 studies of healthy subjects resting recumbent (Williams, 1994), per paragraph 311.

kidney_blood_flow_fraction_adult_male.location: Table 2.40 (printed page 29, PDF page 43); Section 7.7.2 table 'Reference values for regional blood volumes and blood flow rates in adults' (PDF page 156)
kidney_blood_flow_fraction_adult_male.quote: Kidneys 19 17 (male, female; blood flow rate, % cardiac output)
kidney_blood_flow_fraction_adult_male.basis: Adopted from Williams and Leggett (1989) and Leggett and Williams (1991, 1995), per the paragraph introducing the table.

red_cell_fraction_of_blood_adult_male.quote: Typically, red blood cells represent about 43% (42–52%) of the total blood volume in adult males and about 38% (37–48%) in adult females (Guyton, 1982; Johnson, 1998).
red_cell_fraction_of_blood_adult_male.use: Taken as the haematocrit to convert blood flow to plasma flow.

renal_blood_flow_ml_min.note: 6.5 L/min x 19% = 1.235 L/min, both kidneys together.

renal_plasma_flow_ml_min.formula: renal blood flow x (1 - red cell fraction)

not_this: Reference physiology for a reference man: not this patient's blood flow, not adjusted for kidney function, age, body size or sex.
